correctness.rationale: The only degree-three irreducible component is the smooth Fermat cubic; its preservation forces preservation of the three-line union defined by x^3+y^3 and its unique concurrence point [0:0:1]. Any point stabilizer fixing that point has first two coordinates depending only on (x,y) and third coordinate ell(x,y)+mu z. Comparing coefficients of z^2 in Fermat equation forces ell=0, and cubic coefficient forces both binary-cubic and z^3 multipliers equal. The binary cubic has 3 distinct roots in P^1, full projective permutation group S3. Its lifts to PGL3 preserving the total Fermat equation have a 3-element kernel, producing exactly 18 monomial/swap maps, structure C3 x S3. Independently enumerating phase-normalized monomial elements reproduced 18. The degree-seven unique extra line not through concurrency point must be fixed, which imposes equal y/z exponents and excludes swaps, leaving precisely 3 maps. This establishes completeness over C rather than only a finite sample.
residual_risks: Calculates only the embedded PGL3(C) stabilizer of exactly these two reduced divisors, not complements or arbitrary flex-line sets.

originality.rationale: The source Talar 2023 presents both explicit free degree-six and seven curves with equations and freeness checks. Their stabilizers are not asserted by the inspected main scientific sections. Dimca–Ilardi–Pokora–Sticlaru 2023 gives a larger Fermat flex-tangent construction, not a calculation of exact embedded stabilizers for these marked line sets. Other published group results for unrelated free conic-line arrangements do not imply these two groups. The componentwise central C3 and symmetric S3 quotient reflect actual flex configuration rather than automatic generic Fermat automorphisms. Classical projectively equivalent descriptions remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: Classical older geometry of Fermat flex configurations under different projective coordinates could contain the identical group computation.

value.rationale: A complete embedded automorphism group is a standard natural geometric invariant of a distinguished free plane divisor. These examples show a precise sixfold symmetry-breaking under addition of one flex tangent, despite preservation of freeness; the direct product central kernel distinguishes componentwise invisibility from the actual S3 permutation of components. It provides a reusable exact symmetry check for two notable examples, not merely an arbitrary coordinate substitution.
residual_risks: Specialized to two displayed divisors; no assertion of broad group classification.

final_claim: For D6 defined by (x^3+y^3+z^3)(x^3+y^3)=0, full embedded complex projective stabilizer is C3 x S3 of order18; for D7 additionally multiplying by (y+z), stabilizer is C3 of order3, a sixfold drop while both source arrangements are free.
